declarations.en: For a normed field $E$ and a sequence $a:ℕ→E_∞$, the definition $\mathrm{TendstoP1}(a,b)$ assigns to each $b∈E_∞$ the proposition $C(a,b)$. Here $E_∞$ is the disjoint union of $E$ with a symbol $∞$, represented by $\mathrm{Option}(E)$; write $[x]$ for a finite value. For a sequence $s:ℕ→E_∞$, $C(s,[β])$ means that for every real $ε>0$, eventually there exists $α∈E$ with $s(n)=[α]$ and $‖α-β‖<ε$; $C(s,∞)$ means that for every $R∈ℝ$, eventually every $α∈E$ with $s(n)=[α]$ satisfies $R<‖α‖$. declarations.en: For a sequence $a:ℕ→E∪{∞}$, write $a→_P b$ to mean the following explicitly: if $b=β∈E$, then for every real $ε>0$ there is $N∈ℕ$ such that, for every $n≥N$, there exists $α∈E$ with $a_n=α$ and $‖α-β‖<ε$; if $b=∞$, then for every $R∈ℝ$ there is $N∈ℕ$ such that, for every $n≥N$ and every $α∈E$, $a_n=α$ implies $R<‖α‖$. Thus $a_n=∞$ imposes no restriction in the latter implication. Let $E$ be any normed field, $a:ℕ→\operatorname{Option}(E)$ any sequence, and $β∈E$. Interpret some $α$ as the finite value $α$, and none as a separate element $∞$. Then $a→_P β$ holds if and only if there exists a sequence $α:ℕ→E$ for which there is $N∈ℕ$ such that $a_n$ is the finite value $α_n$ for all $n≥N$, and $α_n$ converges to $β$ in the norm topology as $n→∞$. The auxiliary sequence is defined at every natural number, including any initial indices where $a_n=∞$; only its tail must represent $a$. No field $K$ or family of places is a parameter of this assertion.

Write $v_x(t)=ψ_x(t)$ when $t∈O_x$, and $v_x(t)=∞$ otherwise; finite values are tagged elements of $E$ and $∞$ is a separate element, corresponding respectively to some and none in $\operatorname{Option}(E)$. For a sequence $a:ℕ→E∪{∞}$, write $a→_P b$ to mean the following explicitly: if $b=β∈E$, then for every real $ε>0$ there is $N∈ℕ$ such that, for every $n≥N$, there exists $α∈E$ with $a_n=α$ and $‖α-β‖<ε$; if $b=∞$, then for every $R∈ℝ$ there is $N∈ℕ$ such that, for every $n≥N$ and every $α∈E$, $a_n=α$ implies $R<‖α‖$. Let $ι$ be a countable nonempty type and $\mathrm{Good}:E→\mathrm{Prop}$ any predicate. Suppose that for every sequence $a:ℕ→E$ whose every term satisfies $\mathrm{Good}$, there exists a strictly increasing $φ:ℕ→ℕ$ such that either there exists $b∈E$ with $a_{φ(n)}→b$ in the norm topology, or $‖a_{φ(n)}‖→+∞$ (for every real $R$, eventually $R≤‖a_{φ(n)}‖$). An $E$-valued place $x$ consists of a subring $O_x⊆K$, containing $0,1$ and closed under addition, multiplication and negation, such that every $t∈K$ satisfies $t∈O_x$ or $t^{-1}∈O_x$, together with a unital ring homomorphism $ψ_x:O_x→E$ such that $ψ_x(u)=0$ if and only if $u$ is not a unit of $O_x$. Write $v_x(t)=ψ_x(t)$ when $t∈O_x$, and $v_x(t)=∞$ otherwise; finite values are tagged elements of $E$ and $∞$ is a separate element, corresponding respectively to some and none in $\operatorname{Option}(E)$. For a sequence $a:ℕ→E∪{∞}$, write $a→_P b$ to mean the following explicitly: if $b=β∈E$, then for every real $ε>0$ there is $N∈ℕ$ such that, for every $n≥N$, there exists $α∈E$ with $a_n=α$ and $‖α-β‖<ε$; if $b=∞$, then for every $R∈ℝ$ there is $N∈ℕ$ such that, for every $n≥N$ and every $α∈E$, $a_n=α$ implies $R<‖α‖$. Thus $a_n=∞$ imposes no restriction in the latter implication. Let $x:ℕ→\operatorname{EPlace}(K,E)$ be a sequence of such places, and let $ξ:K→E∪{∞}$ be a function. Assume the hypothesis $h$: for every $t∈K$, the sequence $n↦v_{x_n}(t)$ satisfies $n↦v_{x_n}(t)→_P ξ(t)$. For every $f∈K$, if $ξ(f)=∞$, then $ξ(f^{-1})=0$ as a finite value. There is no separately stated nonzero premise on $f$.

declarations.en: Let $K$ be any countable field of characteristic zero, let $E$ be any normed field, and let $\mathrm{Good}$ be any predicate on $E$; the types underlying $K$ and $E$ may lie in arbitrary universes. Assume that for every sequence $a:\mathbb N\to E$ satisfying $\mathrm{Good}(a(n))$ for every $n$, there is a strictly increasing map $\varphi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that either there exists $b\in E$ with $a(\varphi(n))\to b$ in the norm topology as $n\to\infty$, or $\|a(\varphi(n))\|\to+\infty$. Under this assumption, let $d$ be any nonzero natural number, put $I_d=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$, and let $y:\mathbb N\to I_d\to\operatorname{EPlace}(K,E)$ be any family. Here each object $y(n,i)$ consists of a valuation subring $O_{n,i}\subseteq K$ and a unital ring homomorphism $\theta_{n,i}:O_{n,i}\to E$ such that, for every $x\in O_{n,i}$, $\theta_{n,i}(x)=0$ if and only if $x$ is not a unit of $O_{n,i}$. A valuation subring is a subring $O$ such that for every $x\in K$, either $x\in O$ or $x^{-1}\in O$; the whole field $K$ is allowed. Its value $v_{n,i}(f)$ for $f\in K$ is the tagged value $\operatorname{some}(\theta_{n,i}(f))$ when $f\in O_{n,i}$, and the additional symbol $\infty$ otherwise; $E\sqcup\{\infty\}$ denotes these tagged finite values and this additional symbol, corresponding to $\operatorname{Option}E$ with $\infty=\operatorname{none}$. Assume that for all $n\in\mathbb N$, $i\in I_d$, $f\in K$, and $\alpha\in E$, the equality $v_{n,i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ implies $\mathrm{Good}(\alpha)$. Then for every strictly increasing map $D_0:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, there exists a strictly increasing map $D:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that there exists a strictly increasing map $\psi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ with $D=D_0\circ\psi$, and there exists a function $\xi:I_d\to K\to E\sqcup\{\infty\}$ with the following property for every $i\in I_d$ and every $f\in K$: if $\xi(i,f)=\operatorname{some}(\beta)$, then for every real $\varepsilon>0$, eventually in $n$ there exists $\alpha\in E$ such that $v_{D(n),i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ and $\|\alpha-\beta\|<\varepsilon$; if $\xi(i,f)=\infty$, then for every real $R$, eventually in $n$, every $\alpha\in E$ satisfying $v_{D(n),i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ satisfies $R<\|\alpha\|$. In the latter case an index at which the value is $\infty$ imposes no condition on a finite value. Here $\mathbb N$ includes zero, strictly increasing means that $m<n$ implies the corresponding strict inequality between images, and “eventually in $n$” means that there exists $N\in\mathbb N$ such that the stated condition holds for every $n\ge N$.
declarations.zh_Hans: 设 $K$ 为任意可数的零特征域，$E$ 为任意赋范域，$\mathrm{Good}$ 为 $E$ 上的任意谓词；$K$ 和 $E$ 的底层类型可以属于任意宇宙。假设对每个满足 $\forall n\in\mathbb N,\ \mathrm{Good}(a(n))$ 的序列 $a:\mathbb N\to E$，都存在严格递增映射 $\varphi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$，使得以下两种情形至少有一种成立：存在 $b\in E$，当 $n\to\infty$ 时，$a(\varphi(n))$ 在范数拓扑下收敛于 $b$；或者 $\|a(\varphi(n))\|\to+\infty$。在此前提下，任取非零自然数 $d$，记 $I_d=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$，并任取族 $y:\mathbb N\to I_d\to\operatorname{EPlace}(K,E)$。这里，每个对象 $y(n,i)$ 由赋值子环 $O_{n,i}\subseteq K$ 和保幺环同态 $\theta_{n,i}:O_{n,i}\to E$ 组成，且对每个 $x\in O_{n,i}$，$\theta_{n,i}(x)=0$ 当且仅当 $x$ 不是 $O_{n,i}$ 的单位。赋值子环指满足下述条件的子环 $O$：对每个 $x\in K$，都有 $x\in O$ 或 $x^{-1}\in O$；允许 $O=K$。对 $f\in K$，若 $f\in O_{n,i}$，其值 $v_{n,i}(f)$ 为带标签的有限值 $\operatorname{some}(\theta_{n,i}(f))$；否则为附加符号 $\infty$。记 $E\sqcup\{\infty\}$ 为这些带标签的有限值与该附加符号组成的集合，对应 $\operatorname{Option}E$，其中 $\infty=\operatorname{none}$。假设对所有 $n\in\mathbb N$、$i\in I_d$、$f\in K$ 和 $\alpha\in E$，等式 $v_{n,i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ 都蕴含 $\mathrm{Good}(\alpha)$。那么，对每个严格递增映射 $D_0:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$，都存在严格递增映射 $D:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$，使得存在严格递增映射 $\psi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ 满足 $D=D_0\circ\psi$，并且存在函数 $\xi:I_d\to K\to E\sqcup\{\infty\}$，对每个 $i\in I_d$ 和每个 $f\in K$ 满足下述条件：若 $\xi(i,f)=\operatorname{some}(\beta)$，则对每个实数 $\varepsilon>0$，当 $n$ 充分大时，存在 $\alpha\in E$，使得 $v_{D(n),i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ 且 $\|\alpha-\beta\|<\varepsilon$；若 $\xi(i,f)=\infty$，则对每个实数 $R$，当 $n$ 充分大时，每个满足 $v_{D(n),i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ 的 $\alpha\in E$ 都满足 $R<\|\alpha\|$。在后一种情形中，值为 $\infty$ 的指标不对有限值施加条件。这里，$\mathbb N$ 包含零；严格递增指 $m<n$ 蕴含相应的像之间也有严格小于关系；“当 $n$ 充分大时”指存在 $N\in\mathbb N$，使得所述条件对所有 $n\ge N$ 成立。
declarations.ja: $K$ を任意の可算な標数零の体、$E$ を任意のノルム体、$\mathrm{Good}$ を $E$ 上の任意の述語とする。$K$ と $E$ の台となる型は任意の宇宙に属してよい。すべての $n\in\mathbb N$ について $\mathrm{Good}(a(n))$ を満たす任意の列 $a:\mathbb N\to E$ に対して、狭義単調増加写像 $\varphi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ が存在し、ある $b\in E$ について $n\to\infty$ のとき $a(\varphi(n))$ がノルム位相で $b$ に収束するか、または $\|a(\varphi(n))\|\to+\infty$ となると仮定する。この仮定の下で、$d$ を任意の零でない自然数とし、$I_d=\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ と置き、任意の族 $y:\mathbb N\to I_d\to\operatorname{EPlace}(K,E)$ を取る。ここで各対象 $y(n,i)$ は、付値部分環 $O_{n,i}\subseteq K$ と単位元を保つ環準同型 $\theta_{n,i}:O_{n,i}\to E$ からなり、すべての $x\in O_{n,i}$ について、$\theta_{n,i}(x)=0$ であることと $x$ が $O_{n,i}$ の単元でないことが同値である。付値部分環とは、すべての $x\in K$ について $x\in O$ または $x^{-1}\in O$ を満たす部分環 $O$ であり、$O=K$ も許される。$f\in K$ における値 $v_{n,i}(f)$ は、$f\in O_{n,i}$ の場合にはタグ付きの有限値 $\operatorname{some}(\theta_{n,i}(f))$、それ以外の場合には追加の記号 $\infty$ である。$E\sqcup\{\infty\}$ はこれらのタグ付き有限値と追加の記号からなる集合を表し、$\operatorname{Option}E$ に対応し、$\infty=\operatorname{none}$ とする。すべての $n\in\mathbb N$、$i\in I_d$、$f\in K$、$\alpha\in E$ について、$v_{n,i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ ならば $\mathrm{Good}(\alpha)$ であると仮定する。このとき、任意の狭義単調増加写像 $D_0:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ に対して、狭義単調増加写像 $D:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ が存在し、ある狭義単調増加写像 $\psi:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ について $D=D_0\circ\psi$ となり、さらに関数 $\xi:I_d\to K\to E\sqcup\{\infty\}$ が存在して、すべての $i\in I_d$ と $f\in K$ について次が成り立つ。$\xi(i,f)=\operatorname{some}(\beta)$ の場合、任意の実数 $\varepsilon>0$ に対して、十分大きいすべての $n$ で、ある $\alpha\in E$ が存在して $v_{D(n),i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ かつ $\|\alpha-\beta\|<\varepsilon$ となる。$\xi(i,f)=\infty$ の場合、任意の実数 $R$ に対して、十分大きいすべての $n$ で、$v_{D(n),i}(f)=\operatorname{some}(\alpha)$ を満たすすべての $\alpha\in E$ について $R<\|\alpha\|$ となる。後者の場合、値が $\infty$ である添字では有限値に対する条件は課されない。ここで $\mathbb N$ は零を含み、狭義単調増加とは $m<n$ ならば像についても対応する狭義不等式が成り立つことをいい、「十分大きいすべての $n$」とは、ある $N\in\mathbb N$ が存在して、すべての $n\ge N$ で述べた条件が成り立つことをいう。
